title: Replacement System Installations: Cancellation After the Cancellation Period and the Restocking Fee
content:
# Cancellation after the cancellation period

## Scope

These terms govern a Replacement System Installations contract cancelled after its cancellation period has ended, and a showroom, phone or web contract cancelled at any time.

## Terms

1. Such a contract is cancelled only while the project is signed or scheduled; once the project is installed it can no longer be cancelled. A cancellation is accepted only while the project status is signed or scheduled.
2. The cancellation charges a cancellation fee of the package's restocking fee percentage of the contract price, rounded to the cent half up.
3. Every other charge on the project, including the permit fee once the permit is pulled, is credited by a cancellation credit naming it.
4. Member, rebate and multi-system credits already posted stay as they are only to the extent they do not exceed the charges they named.
5. The homeowner's payments, then the lender's disbursement, are applied to the cancellation fee, and anything paid beyond it is refunded under the refund rules.
6. A cancellation with nothing paid leaves the cancellation fee owing.

The charges the cancellation credits are the project's charges other than the cancellation fee, less every credit already applied to them, over the project's life to the date of handling.

## Status table

| Project status | Cancellation accepted |
|---|---|
| Signed | Yes |
| Scheduled | Yes |
| Installed, inspected or closed | No |

## Worked example (hypothetical project)

A hypothetical showroom contract at $12695.00 on a package with a 15 percent restocking fee is cancelled while scheduled, after a $1904.25 deposit and with a $112.00 permit-fee charge posted.

- Cancellation fee: 15 percent of $12695.00 is $1904.25.
- The contract-price charge and the $112.00 permit-fee charge are each credited by a cancellation credit naming them.
- The $1904.25 deposit is applied to the cancellation fee, which leaves nothing paid beyond the fee and nothing to refund.

Had the homeowner paid nothing, the $1904.25 cancellation fee would remain owing.
